standard.title: Protective behaviours and help-seeking
standard.description: identify and demonstrate protective behaviours and help-seeking strategies they can use to help them and others stay safe
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have demonstrated protective behaviours, named body parts and rehearsed help-seeking strategies that help keep them safe (AC9HPFP05).
standard.progression_endpoint: Students identify and demonstrate protective behaviours and help-seeking strategies to help them and others stay safe.

nodes.label: Body reactions to safe and unsafe situations
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify the body's reaction to safe and unsafe situations and compare the different emotional responses.
nodes.minimum_width: Describe how their body feels in a safe situation versus an unsafe or uncomfortable situation; identify this as a signal to act.
nodes.typical_width: Identify the body's physical and emotional reactions to a range of safe and unsafe situations; explain how these reactions can help them recognise when they need to use protective behaviours.
wider: Explore how characters in texts experience safe and unsafe situations and compare their emotional responses to the student's own experience
Identify body reactions in emergency scenarios through role play and describe what these signals mean
Compare how the same situation might feel different to different people, and discuss what this means for recognising when others may need help
nodes.hinge_reason: Recognising bodily and emotional signals as safety indicators is the conceptual anchor for all protective and help-seeking action. Students who do not understand the signal cannot reliably trigger the protective response in real situations.

response_modes.reason: Use explicit language scaffolds to connect body signals to meaning: 'When I feel __ in my body, it might mean __'. This prevents the concept staying at the level of emotion labelling rather than signal interpretation.

success_criteria: Describes at least one body reaction that signals a safe situation and one that signals an unsafe situation
Identifies these reactions as signals to consider a protective response

nodes.label: Help-seeking strategies and safe networks
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify and rehearse strategies they can use when requiring assistance, including trusted adults, safe places and problem-solving with friends.
nodes.minimum_width: Name at least one trusted adult and one safe place they could go to for help; describe one strategy for asking for help.
nodes.typical_width: Identify a network of trusted people and safe places; practise strategies for seeking help including asking an adult, reading signs, recognising safe locations, and problem-solving with friends.
wider: Recognise photos and locations of safe places in the school and local community and explain why these are safe
Explore how to seek help in different scenarios — at school, at home, and in public — and compare which strategies are most appropriate in each context
Discuss the importance of seeking help when a problem is too big to solve alone, and practise how to communicate the nature of the problem to a trusted adult

response_modes.reason: Students need a practical repertoire of help-seeking strategies and a named network of trusted people. Build this explicitly — not all students have clear networks or know how to activate them.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Help-seeking strategies across multiple contexts (school, home, public) and through multiple channels (trusted people, safe places, problem-solving with friends) build a meaningfully wider safety repertoire. Students with only one strategy or one trusted contact have a thin safety network.
success_criteria: Names at least one trusted adult and one safe place they could access for help
Describes at least one strategy for asking for help in a situation

nodes.label: Protective behaviours including digital safety
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify and rehearse protective behaviours, including strategies for safe use of digital tools.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least one protective behaviour for a physical safety context and one for digital tool use; practise or describe each.
nodes.typical_width: Identify and rehearse a range of protective behaviours across physical and digital contexts; explain how these behaviours help them and others stay safe.
wider: Propose strategies for healthy and manageable use of digital tools at school and home and explain how these protect wellbeing
Explore how to respond to uncomfortable or unsafe situations in digital spaces and compare these strategies to responses in physical situations
Role-play using protective behaviours in a range of scenarios drawn from stories, everyday life and online contexts

response_modes.reason: This node connects body-signal awareness (Node 1) and help-seeking strategies (Node 2) into the full protective behaviour repertoire, extended to digital contexts. Tasks should require students to identify a signal, select a protective behaviour and identify a help-seeking path — not treat each as a separate skill.

success_criteria: Identifies at least one protective behaviour for a physical safety situation
Identifies at least one protective behaviour for safe digital tool use
